# Iddhibalakathā (Kv 11.5)

**ID:** Kv 11.5
**Section:** Kathāvatthu (kv)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Iddhibalakathā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh03m3.mul18.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Iddhibalakathā* (Kv 11.5) is a debate located in the eleventh chapter (*vagga*) of the Abhidhamma treatise *Kathāvatthu*. The controversy examines the proposition of whether an individual endowed with psychic or supernormal power (*iddhibala*) can survive or remain for an entire cosmic age (*kappa*) [Bareau 1955; La Vallée Poussin, Conciles bouddhiques]. While scriptural passages record the Buddha stating that one who has developed and mastered the four bases of psychic power (*iddhipāda*) could remain for a *kappa* if desired, the orthodox Theravāda argument counters that lifespan (*āyu*), destiny (*gati*), and personality are not created by *iddhi*; psychic force cannot render conditioned aggregates (*khandha*) permanent (*nicca*) or prevent mortal and aging phenomena from dying and decaying [Bareau 1955; La Vallée Poussin, Conciles bouddhiques]. Louis de La Vallée Poussin notes that this debate emerged early in Buddhist dogmatics to harmonize scriptural statements regarding life-prolonging psychic powers with the doctrine of universal impermanence [La Vallée Poussin, Conciles bouddhiques].
